cst.banner.description: Wall banner for a wall socket (wall-face anchor, front +Z): an original heraldic hanging (band atlas) with a pointed tail, on a turned pole with gilt finials and an iron bracket.

cst.battlement.description: Crenellated parapet strip on a cell edge (4 m along X) for keep roofs, towers and wall tops: merlons on a parapet with a dressed coping; machicolated kind corbels the parapet out over a row of brackets.

cst.brazier.description: Standing iron brazier: a hammered bowl of burning coals on three splayed legs (fire glows, baked warm pool).

cst.carpet.description: Woven runner carpet (quilt role: dark border, pale stripe, diamond medallions) with a bevelled edge.

cst.ceiling.description: Hall ceiling (one-sided, facing down, N64 cutaway-friendly): dark boards on arched oak trusses across the span, or a stone barrel vault with transverse ribs.

cst.cell.description: Dungeon cell on one grid cell (4 x 4 m, open side toward -Y): rubble back and side walls, an iron-barred front with a barred door (closed / swung open), straw on the floor and wall shackles.

cst.chandelier.description: Iron ring chandelier hung on chains from the ceiling (origin at the hook, hangs down -Z): candles glow, baked warm pool on its own iron.

cst.curtain.description: Castle curtain wall on a cell edge (4 m along X, outer face toward -Y): battered rubble footing, dressed ashlar face, a wall walk with a crenellated outer parapet and a string course; kinds with arrow slits, a ruined broken top, or an inner stair up to the walk. wall_end sockets (curtain) at +-2 m.

cst.dais.description: Stepped stone dais for a throne (one cell deep, cells_x wide): dressed flagstone treads with pale nosings and a carpet strip down the middle steps.

cst.drawbridge.description: Drawbridge for the gatehouse (drawbridge socket anchor, extending toward -Y over the moat): heavy plank deck on iron-strapped beams with hauling chains; lowered flat across the moat or raised upright against the gate. A state pair for module gates.

cst.gatehouse.description: Castle gate block spanning two cell edges (8 m along X, centred on a cell corner, outer face toward -Y): ashlar masses on a battered footing around a pointed-arch passage with a dressed voussoir surround, a portcullis slot, a corbelled machicolation (or plain crenellation) over the arch, and an inner wall at the end of the passage with a door cut and stone arch. Flanking towers are cst.tower_round / cst.tower_square on the end corners. Sockets: wall_end (curtain / tower) at +-4 m, portcullis in the passage mouth, drawbridge in front over the moat, the inner door (a region door takes vlg.doorway).

cst.hall.description: Castle hall shell on the room grid (keep hall, throne room, dungeon passage): ashlar walls on a rubble plinth with pilasters on cell boundaries and a dressed string course, flagstone floor with a pale border, door cuts with stone arch surrounds for vlg.doorway, tall painted lancets, torch sockets with warm baked pools.

cst.keep.description: Castle keep: a great square tower with a battered rubble base, ashlar walls, a string course, lancet windows, a pointed main door with a stone surround, a crenellated parapet and four corbelled corner turrets with conical slate roofs. Door socket on the south face (a region door takes vlg.doorway).

cst.pillar.description: Hall pillar: moulded base and capital with a round, square or clustered shaft (ashlar), pale dressed stone.

cst.portcullis.description: Portcullis for the gatehouse passage (portcullis socket anchor): an iron-shod oak grid with spiked feet, lowered or hauled up into the slot (only the spikes show). A state pair for module gates.

cst.sconce.description: Wall torch for a torch socket (wall-face anchor, front +Z): an iron bracket and a pitch torch with a flame (the shell bakes the pool; the runtime emitter flickers).

cst.spiral_stair.description: Newel (spiral) stair for a tower or keep corner: wedge stone steps winding up around a central newel inside a low drum wall, rising counter-clockwise (one cell).

cst.throne.description: Throne: a tall gilded-oak chair with a pointed crest back, carved arm posts with gilt finials, a red cushion and seat back panel; canopy kind adds a cloth tester on two posts.

cst.tower_round.description: Round castle tower on a cell corner: battered rubble base, ashlar drum with string courses and arrow slits, either a corbelled crenellated parapet or a flared conical slate roof with a heraldic pennant. Curtain wall_end sockets at 2 m on all four axes.

cst.tower_square.description: Square castle tower on a cell corner: battered rubble footing, ashlar shaft with quoins and slits, a crenellated parapet on corbel courses or a pyramid slate roof with a pennant. Curtain sockets at 2 m on four axes.

mnat.bush.description: Shrub: a round bush, a flowering bush, a berry bush, or a low tangled bramble.

mnat.dead_tree.description: Leafless tree: a gnarled trunk splitting into crooked bare branches (winter / spooky), optionally snow-laden.

mnat.field.description: Farm field on the grid (cells x cells, origin at the centre, ground at y = 0): standing wheat as a golden bevelled mass with a ragged top, rows of cabbages, ploughed furrows, or a vineyard of staked rows.

mnat.flowers.description: Small ground dressing: a patch of meadow flowers, grass tufts, waterside reeds, or a ring of mushrooms.

mnat.hedgerow.description: Hedgerow on a cell edge (4 m along X): a clipped-but-lumpy hedge, a corner turning south, or a hedge with a field gap. wall_end sockets (hedge) at +-2 m so hedges, fences and walls interlock.

mnat.oak.description: Oak: a stout tapered trunk with two limbs under a broad crown of four lumpy foliage masses (broad), a slim young oak, or an old pollarded oak with a thicker trunk and a lower, wider crown.

mnat.orchard.description: Orchard fruit tree: a short crooked trunk under a rounded crown dotted with fruit (apple / pear), in blossom, or bare winter branches.

mnat.pine.description: Pine / fir: a straight trunk under stacked drooping tiers of needles (foliage role), tall or short; the snowy kind caps every tier with snow.

mnat.rock.description: Rocks: a mossy boulder, a cluster of three, a tall weathered standing stone, or a low layered outcrop.

mnat.stump.description: A sawn tree stump with root flares, a fallen log, or a mossy log with a fungus shelf.

mprop.anvil.description: Blacksmith's anvil with a horn and heel on an oak stump, optionally with tongs and hammer.

mprop.barrel.description: Oak barrel with two iron hoops: upright, lying on its side, a small keg, or an open water butt.

mprop.basket.description: Woven wicker basket (wattle role) with apples, loaves or wool, or empty.

mprop.bed.description: Bed: a plank cot with a straw mattress, blanket and pillow, or a four-poster with a cloth tester.

mprop.bench.description: Seating: a plank bench, a three-legged stool, or a high-backed settle.

mprop.bucket.description: Wooden pail with two iron bands and a rope handle, optionally full of water.

mprop.cart.description: Two-wheeled farm cart: plank bed with side boards, spoked-look wheels, shafts resting on the ground, loaded with hay, barrels or sacks, or empty.

mprop.cauldron.description: Iron cauldron hung from a tripod over a ring of stones, with a glowing fire (baked warm pool).

mprop.chest.description: Treasure / travel chest: oak body with a rounded lid, iron straps and a lock plate (iron) or plain boards; the lid shut or thrown open (a state pair for module flags).

mprop.crate.description: Plank crate with corner battens and a diagonal brace (braced), an open-slatted produce crate, or a small box.

mprop.grindstone.description: Treadle grindstone: a sandstone wheel on an oak frame with a crank and a water trough.

mprop.hay.description: Straw: a tied bale, a stack of three bales, or a domed hay rick on a timber base.

mprop.lantern.description: Lamp post: an oak post (on a stone footing) with an iron bracket and a glowing lantern cage; its warm pool is baked into its own vertices.

mprop.lantern_hung.description: Hung lanterns: a wall lantern on an iron bracket (wall-face anchor, front +Z, for lantern sockets) or a lantern hanging on a chain (origin at the ceiling hook). The cage glows; its warm pool is baked into its own vertices.

mprop.sack.description: Tied burlap sack (pale cloth), a pile of three, or an open sack of grain.

mprop.shelf.description: Wall shelf (wall-face anchor, front +Z): two oak boards on brackets carrying jugs and bowls, or books.

mprop.shield.description: Wall shield (wall-face anchor, front +Z): a heater or round shield carrying an original heraldic charge (band atlas), with a dark rim.

mprop.signpost.description: Signposts with BLANK faces (paper role, never text: games paint their own): a fingerpost with pointed arms, a post with a hanging board on a bracket, or a little roofed notice board.

mprop.table.description: Tavern / hall table: a trestle table, a round table on a post and feet, or a long feast table.

mprop.tableware.description: Table dressing: a trencher with bread and a jug (meal), tankards round a pitcher (drinks), or a pair of lit candlesticks (baked warm pool).

mprop.trough.description: Hollowed log / plank trough on two blocks, filled with water or hay.

mprop.weapon_rack.description: Armoury rack: an oak frame holding spears, swords, or round shields with original heraldic charges.

mprop.woodpile.description: Firewood: a stacked log pile against two stakes, or a chopping block with split logs and an axe.

mter.backdrop.description: Far backdrop (origin at the viewer): an inward-facing band of rolling hills (vista role) in front of a far ridge (vista_far) that carries two original castle silhouettes (square keep with corner turrets, a round tower pair with a curtain), or a jagged mountain range. View-plane roles, so they take the sky colours of every variant.

mter.bank.description: Terrace edge on a cell edge (4 m along X; the high side toward +Y): a grassy bank, a rock face with a grass lip, or a rubble retaining wall with a coping. Pairs with vlg.stairs for level changes.

mter.ground.description: Ground tile, one 4 m cell (or a plain cells x cells block) (origin at the centre, top at y = 0): grass meadow, cobbles, dirt, flagstone plaza, snow, or a field edge; optionally crossed by a cobbled path (straight / corner / tee / cross / end) that meets the next tile on the cell-edge midpoints. Path sockets on every path end.

mter.hill.description: Rolling hill: a smooth cosine mound on a coarse grid (grass on gentle slopes, rock on the steep ones), skirt at y = 0 so it sits on any ground tile.

mter.water.description: Water on the grid: a river reach across one cell (4 m along X) with grassy banks, a castle moat segment with rubble revetments, or a round pond with a reed-and-stone rim (water role scrolls).

sky.backdrop.description: Sky backdrop: inward-facing dome or cylinder (kit_shell_sky, role 'sky', v = elevation 0..1). Origin at the viewer; extends below y=0 by below_horizon*radius.

vlg.bridge.description: Bridge spanning two cells (8 m, along X): a humpbacked rubble arch bridge with cobbled deck and parapets, or a timber footbridge on trestles with hand rails. Path sockets at both ends.

vlg.ceiling.description: Beamed ceiling for vlg.room (one-sided, facing down so N64 cutaway cameras see in): dark boards on heavy oak joists across the short span (origin on the cell block centre at FLOOR level, like vlg.room).

vlg.chapel.description: Village chapel: rubble nave with dressed quoins and buttresses, steep slate roof, pointed-arch door, lancet windows of leaded glass, a rounded apse and a gable bell-cote with a bell under a simple cross.

vlg.cottage.description: Village cottage in four original styles on a 2 m lattice lot: tapered walls, adzed oak framing as separate bevelled beams, a lofted roof with rolled eaves and a sagging ridge (thick bulging thatch, slate or clay pantiles), plank door with a painted leaf, glass panes (glow at night), rubble plinth and chimney. Door socket on the threshold.

vlg.doorway.description: THE medieval door (styles bind room.gd's arch.door to it): adzed oak frame with a lintel, a plank leaf with iron straps (painted leaf), a stone threshold; origin on the room.gd door anchor (0.4 m in from the room edge), front +Z toward the room, sized for the DOOR_CUT of every MEDIEVALKIT wall and the doorway mode of every building.

vlg.fence.description: Fence on a cell edge (4 m along X): woven wattle hurdles between stakes, post-and-rail, a dry-stone wall with capstones, or a rail fence with a field gate. wall_end sockets at +-2 m.

vlg.gatehouse.description: Village gatehouse spanning a 3.2 m arched passage: rubble piers, deep voussoir arch, jettied timber room above with a roof; plank gate leaves closed or swung open (a state pair). wall_end sockets at +-3.5 m meet vlg.wall segments.

vlg.hearth.description: Inglenook hearth for a hearth socket (wall-face anchor, front +Z): rubble cheeks, an oak bressumer under a plastered chimney breast rising to the ceiling, flagstone hearth slab, burning logs (fire glows, baked warm).

vlg.mill.description: Village mill: a tapered whitewashed tower mill with a stone footing, thatched cap and four lattice sails, or a rubble watermill with a paddle wheel on its gable.

vlg.room.description: Timber-framed interior shell on the room grid (3.4 m storey): whitewashed panels between oak studs on cell boundaries, a mid rail and a plank skirting, plank floor with a flagstone border, door cuts for vlg.doorway, painted windows, hearth and lantern sockets with warm baked pools. Ceilings are separate (vlg.ceiling).

vlg.smithy.description: Village smithy: rubble forge-house with a slate roof and an open-fronted lean-to workshop on timber posts, a stone forge with a glowing fire bed (baked warm pool), hood and tall chimney.

vlg.stairs.description: Exterior steps up a terrace (rising toward +Y / north): rubble flight with dressed treads and side cheeks, or an open timber stair with stringers. Path sockets at the foot and the head.

vlg.stall.description: Market stall: plank counter on four posts under a sloping striped awning with a hanging valance, dressed with goods (produce crates, folded cloth, pots or loaves).

vlg.tavern.description: Two-storey village inn: rubble ground floor, jettied whitewashed upper storey with oak framing and braces, deep clay-tile (or thatch / slate) roof, external stone chimney, a projecting bracket with a BLANK sign board, a door lantern baked warm, wide tap-room windows. Door socket on the threshold.

vlg.wall.description: Town wall segment on a cell edge (4 m along X, origin on the boundary): rubble wall with a coping and wall-walk merlons, a postern with a door socket, corner and end pieces, or a sharpened log palisade. wall_end sockets at +-2 m interlock segments, towers and the gatehouse.

vlg.well.description: Village well: round rubble well-head with a dressed coping, still water inside, two oak posts carrying a windlass with rope and bucket under a little pitched roof.

note: Every GLB here exists for consumers only with this sha256 (explicit sRGB8, converted after the kit validators and the MEDIEVALKIT gates ran on the linear build; source_sha256 = validated build). textures are relative to kits/library/.
